text: GPU is an RTX 4090 (24 GB), not the plan's RTX A4500; exp29 engine-d outcomes came from an RTX 2000 Ada. Same bf16 weights/code path (exp29 engines.load_b, F.linear, CPU embedding gather), different cuBLAS kernels; measured by Stage 0.
Batch sizes B = 24 (T10, T03) and 16 (T2, T1) instead of exp29's B = 7; every arm of a task uses the same B (CRN pairing exact within this engine).

Stage 0c: realised S-mean displacement norms of directions 9101-9105 match exp29 within 0.003% (block 12) and 0.27% (block 23) but differ by up to 2.35% at block 35 (> 2%); pre-declared fallback 1 executed: all 40 directions re-measured at N = 10 on T10/T2 in this engine (sealed until commit #3); primary stays exp29 engine d as committed.

commit #0 (rules, thresholds, input hashes) was written after the Stage 0 code; the analysis drivers (analysis7.py, analysis_push.py, top5geo.py, stats7.py, predict7.py, ...) were frozen by hash in amendment commit0b before commit #3; no POP outcome row was readable before commit #3 (guarded_e29_rows).

Opening classifier: import-only evidence (from collections import deque / import heapq) removed because pushed programs import unused modules (13.6% of exp29 Dijkstra programs import deque); BFS via .pop(0) added. Agreement with the frozen labels on all non-POP labelled programs: T2 0.996 (761), T10 0.998 (1511), T03 1.000 (1235 committed, 15 abstain); stratified 200-program validation 1.0 on all three.

T03 pushed base paths (exp30 ST S0 alpha 2 with exp30's ban-free unit) were not used: porting the exp23 r_Q unit for resampling did not fit the budget; all T03 non-default base paths are BAN paths (6 quickselect, 6 size_k_heap).

commit1_forks was written by code that had not yet run the pre-declared 128-token window extension; commit1b adds it (T2: one off-default change at token 92 on a pushed path, none on the default path; T03: none). commit1c removes a 2-token fork-merge rule (it hid T10's second fork ' def' -> ' find'/' dfs') and adds the sequential multi-fork rule (q_j of the default-path token is 0 at every fork but the last). All amendments precede every margin and predictor.

A1 forced-runner-up prompts are prompts4 'named' prompts F0-F9 (display-name variant 0; K = 10) instead of re-built exp8/exp11 frames; T2's F0 is sha256-identical to exp30's FORCED prompt and T10 bfs F0 to exp30's T10 FORCED prompt.
Natural-variance (dormant-subspace) check uses 10 neutral prompts per task (W1-W5 twins + exp30 placebo twins, i.e. 2 nouns per template) instead of 3 nouns x 5 templates.
P2 secondary DAS skipped (drop item 5) to keep the never-drop items inside the budget.

T1 10-algorithm labels come from exp9 labeller_ext AST rules only (exp9's runtime tracer probes were not ported); the frozen exp8 runtime+AST 6-class label and the hidden-test pass flag are kept beside it.
Tier-3 margin cells COND (KV splice), RPOS and MR (per-sample random exchange) were not computed; X_24-35, X_0-11 and PLACEBO were.

CPU test C3 fails as specified: with only 3 pre-jump screen positions (t = 0, 4, 8) a 0.4 jump is detected at p < 0.01 in 54% of simulations (0.3: 35%, 0.2: 7%; null 0%). The screen is underpowered for very early forks; weak forks can be missed.

L_geo = block 18 (exp30's F5 figure layer is not recorded in its npz, which holds S-means of blocks 12-23; block 18 is iteration 4's GEO_BLOCKS[0]); geometry is also reported at L_ax(T1) = median of the three tasks' L_ax.
T1 forced prompts for the 10-algorithm catalogue: exp9 frozen_prompts 'forced:X' (10 paraphrases each, plain condition), built in the prompts4 chat frame (spec ids asserted identical to the twins').

Targeted push never escaped at s <= 1 on T10, T2, T03 (claim fails as committed); pre-declared fallback 8 adds s in {2, 4} (descriptive, N = 30, same CRN slots) and s = 8 (beyond the plan, because rho_s at s = 1 was 0.13-0.18, i.e. the escaping random directions realise 5.6-8x the s = 1 displacement at L_ax).

Geodesic g(X) and the edge/opposite split use the smallest Isomap k in {5,10,15} whose kNN graph is connected (k = 15 at both layers; k = 5 and 10 are disconnected). Decided from the forced-prompt geometry alone, before any T1 landing label was read; the k sweep is reported.

Analysis code changed after commit0b: (1) analysis7/analysis_push/outputs7 read the latest commit-#3 file via c7.c3_path() and predict7 the latest fork file (before any outcome row was opened; commit3b); (2) top5geo uses the smallest connected Isomap k for g(X) (after the forced-prompt geometry, before any T1 landing label was read; D-isomap-k); (3) analysis_push adds the fallback-8 descriptive doses s = 2, 4, 8 (after the committed s <= 1 result was seen; descriptive only); (4) figures7/readme7/outputs7 presentation changes and the exploratory scripts (explore_llr, force_token, analysis_force) after the committed results. Every committed statistic is computed by the code hashed in commit0b except for change (1), which only selects the amended input file.

GPU test U5 misses its 0.05 tolerance: teacher-forced (use_cache=False) and KV-prefill log-probs differ by up to 0.25 on the top-50 tokens (argmax equal) because the two SDPA paths round differently in bf16; all margins use the same teacher-forced path, so cells are comparable.

CPU test C6: the AST-only exp9 labeller_ext agrees with the adjudicated exp9 T1 gold labels on 32/40 programs (0.80); T1 conclusions (every push arm BFS 30/30) agree with the frozen exp8 runtime+AST 6-class label on every row.

Exploratory forced-token test shows the T10 token map is cell-dependent for non-committal tokens (' #' has q = 1.00 pooled over ban/PN cells but gives union-find 30/30 under the twin); the committed margin pools q over cells as specified, which limits F.

Portability edits after the analysis: src/dep7.py reads the dependency art_j3Rm_lr2nzR6 through AII_DEP_ART_J3RM (default: the sibling folder ../art_j3Rm_lr2nzR6) instead of an absolute server path; src/axis7.py's seed-disjointness scan reads extra roots from AII_EARLIER_ARTIFACT_ROOTS (default: the vendored copies). No result changes (the committed scan is recorded in commit #2).
